- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in that window.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 3–5 day horizons; if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast should be capped at 10–15% below that average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon; apply a 5–10% downward correction for days 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to forecast adjustment.
